title: Apple Completes the Set: Every Magnificent Seven Stock Opts Out of OKX-ICE Venue
detail:
Apple Completes the Set: Every Magnificent Seven Stock Opts Out of OKX-ICE Venue
Decrypt Staff
Sat, November 7, 2026 at 11:01 AM CST 2 min read
META
AAPL
MSFT
GOOG
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Every member of Wall Street's "Magnificent Seven" now wants its stock kept off OKX and ICE's planned tokenized stock venue.

Apple and Meta Platforms are among 11 companies added to the list of objecting issuers in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Thursday.

They join Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia and Tesla, completing a sweep by the group of tech giants that makes up a large share of the S&P 500's value. The other new objectors are Home Depot, Boeing, GE Vernova, Palantir, ServiceNow, S&P Global, KLA, Super Micro Computer and Nebius Group, bringing the total number of companies saying "no" to the OKX and ICE platform to 67.

Meta's objection carries some irony. The Facebook parent once tried to launch its own stablecoin, Libra, later renamed Diem, before abandoning the project in 2022 amid regulatory pushback.

Apple had been one of the last megacaps missing from the list after Amazon, Tesla, and SpaceX objected in the venue's Nov. 2 notice. The tally stood at 56 then, and at nine on Oct. 15, when the first objectors appeared.

Just as notable is who hasn't objected. Crypto-friendly public companies such as Coinbase, Robinhood and Strategy don't appear on the list. Coinbase launched tokenized stocks for non-U.S. users on its Base network in August. Berkshire Hathaway, Visa, and Exxon Mobil are also absent. It's unclear whether OKXICE notified those companies.

Under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act failed to advance in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can't make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC's order. It's worth noting, though, that the objection applies only to that venue.

OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, plans to offer tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain. An outside "tokenizer" would hold real shares one-for-one through a registered broker-dealer.

With the market's biggest names opted out, it's unclear which major stocks the venue will be able to offer at launch, and its notices don't list the tokens it plans to make available.

title: CoreWeave’s Bonds Now Yield More Than 16%, Days Before Earnings
detail:
CoreWeave’s Bonds Now Yield More Than 16%, Days Before Earnings
Omor Ibne Ehsan
Sat, November 7, 2026 at 9:37 AM CST 5 min read
CRWV
MSFT
NVDA
AMZN
ORCL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

CoreWeave's 2032 bond yields over 16% against a 10% coupon, signaling lenders doubt it can keep refinancing before its November 10 earnings.

Microsoft supplied roughly 67% of CoreWeave's 2025 revenue, while it winds down an Oracle rental deal and trims its smaller neocloud suppliers.

Credit stress is rising at NVIDIA and Amazon too, yet levels remain low, so the strain stays concentrated on the weakest borrower.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

On November 6, 2026, the 2032 bond of CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) traded at a yield above 16%, even though it pays a coupon of only 9.625%. Lenders usually ask for that kind of return only when they doubt a company can keep refinancing.

24/7 Wall St.

The bond move followed a jump in the cost of insuring CoreWeave's debt. A credit default swap works like an insurance policy: the buyer pays an annual premium and collects if the borrower defaults. Five-year protection rose above 1,289 basis points on November 5, which works out to an annual premium of about 12.9% of the debt insured. It then fell about 8% to around 1,155 basis points on November 6.

The stock moved in the opposite direction. Shares fell 9.83% on November 5 to $43.66, then traded at $46.40 late on November 6, up 6.28%. That bounce had no clear link to the bond market.

Third-quarter results are scheduled for November 10 after the close. Right now, bondholders and stock analysts are pricing two very different companies, and that report is the first real test of which group is right.

Why a 16% Yield Raises Borrowing Costs

A bond that yields far more than its coupon trades well below face value, because buyers will hold it only at a discount large enough to lift their return. In mid-October, the $1.25 billion issue traded at 15% and closed at 14.5%. It now yields more than it did then.

title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Just Issued a 6-Word Warning That Could Spell Disaster for AI Stocks

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Just Issued a 6-Word Warning That Could Spell Disaster for AI Stocks

MSFT

Quick Read

CoreWeave and Nebius plunged about 47% and 45% in a month as rate pressure hit debt-funded AI data center builders.

Microsoft's $19 billion in free cash flow lets it build without borrowing, while Alphabet turned to $29 billion in new bonds.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warned "Interest rates get in the cracks," and markets see a 72% chance of another December hike.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

On October 28, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh summed up the AI market's weak spot in six words: "Interest rates get in the cracks." Then he added: "Interest rates affect directly or indirectly almost everything." That includes the AI data center buildout, and a large share of it is paid for with borrowed money.

24/7 Wall St.

In the month ending November 6, CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) fell 47.54% and Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) dropped 45.4%. Over the same month, Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) edged up 0.16%. The market now sorts AI companies by one question: who pays for data centers with cash, and who borrows to build them?

Two Rate Squeezes Hitting at Once

The Fed raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point in September and held it at 3.75% to 4.00% in October. As of November 3, CME FedWatch put the odds of another quarter-point hike in December at 72%. Long-term rates are adding a second pressure. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.24% on October 9 and still stood at 4.84% on November 5. That same day, the VIX volatility index rose to 28.18, its highest reading since early August.

Borrowers Are Feeling It First

CoreWeave shows the problem most clearly. Its revenue backlog is $104.2 billion, but to deliver it the company plans to spend $35 billion to $39 billion on capital projects this year, and its debt is 8.94 times its equity. Second-quarter interest expense was $640 million, up from $267 million a year earlier. Management expects $860 million to $940 million in the third quarter.

title: What Is Behind The Move In Atlassian Stock?
detail:
What Is Behind The Move In Atlassian Stock?
Trefis Team

TEAM

Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Atlassian (TEAM) stock fell 16.2% on Friday, November 6, 2026, while the S&P 500 rose 0.3%. After the close on Thursday, November 5, the company reported first-quarter results for fiscal 2027 that beat analysts' estimates for both earnings and revenue. So why did a quarter that beat estimates send the shares this far down?

Atlassian Beat Estimates But Expects Slower Cloud Growth

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Atlassian earned an adjusted $1.65 per share, compared to the $1.39 analysts expected. Revenue reached $1.8 billion, above the $1.71 billion estimate, and management said on the November 5 call that cloud revenue grew 31%.

The shares fell on what Atlassian said about cloud growth. While the company raised its outlook for the full year, its guidance pointed to slower cloud growth, and the stock sold off as soon as the numbers came out. On the call, an analyst said the second-quarter cloud revenue guide implied about 4 points of slowdown, more than the guidance from 90 days earlier had implied. Some analysts called the worry over slower cloud growth an overreaction.

Management stressed other figures on the call. RPO, representing revenue customers have signed up for but Atlassian has not yet booked, grew 44% to $4.7 billion. More than 3,000 customers have now upgraded to the Teamwork Collection, seven times as many as a year earlier.

Did Other Software Stocks Fall With Atlassian?

Atlassian's software peers also fell, though by far less, even as the wider technology sector rose. The technology sector fund XLK gained 1.5% in the same session. Among the companies on the Trefis list of Atlassian's peers, Asana fell 5.0% and Salesforce fell 3.9%.

Asana saw the largest of those peer falls, yet its decline was less than a third of Atlassian's drop. Atlassian's stock moved on its own report, not with its group.

One report can knock a single stock down 16.2%. Here's how to build a portfolio for a crash and a rally.

Where Does Atlassian Stock Stand Now?

Over the prior 365 days, Atlassian had not fallen this much in a single session. Its last move this large went the other way: a 35.3% gain on August 7, 2026.

The drop leaves the shares down 4.8% over the past 12 months, against a 9.8% gain for the S&P 500. Friday's close of $153.68 sits well below the stock's highest close of the year, $227.61 on October 23, 2026, but remains far above the year's lowest close, $57.15 on April 10, 2026. The stock returned 67.8% over the past six months, yet it fell 24.5% over the past month alone.

Big Tech's $1 Trillion Rally Bets Regulation Won't Touch "the Profits of the Tech Companies" ©Worawee Meepian's Images and Yakobchuk from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta were on pace to add nearly $1 trillion on Wednesday after Democrats won Congress. On Thursday, the four hyperscalers gave back 2% to 4%.

New York Assemblymember Alex Bores says investors bet on tight limits on new data centers and no rules that hit Big Tech's profits.

Trump's veto threat makes new federal AI laws unlikely before 2029. California's governor-elect is a separate risk.

Microsoft trades near its one-year average forward P/E, leaving little room for rules that cut expected profits.

On Nov. 4, investors cheered the Democratic sweep by piling into Big Tech. Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ), Alphabet (GOOG), Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) and Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ), along with Apple, were on pace to add nearly $1 trillion in market value, by Bloomberg's count, and Microsoft closed at a record.

Democrats ran on slowing the AI build-out. Investors read that as a brake on the spending that has pushed free cash flow negative at Amazon, Alphabet and Meta. Neoclouds like CoreWeave sank.

On the Nov. 5 episode of Prof G Markets, Alex Bores, a New York Assembly member and author of the RAISE Act, said the move "expresses a bet that there will be stringent regulation on building new data centers, that that capacity will be curtailed, but that there won't be regulations that impact the profits of the tech companies and the AI companies."

He doesn't buy the second half, saying it doesn't match what he hears from voters or elected officials.

By Thursday, the mood had turned. The Nasdaq 100 fell about 6% in a broad chip and AI selloff, and the four hyperscalers gave back 2% to 4% each.

Big Tech Has a Lot of Profit to Protect

The money at stake is the earnings growth Wall Street already expects. Consensus has Alphabet's normalized EPS rising from $10.81 in 2025 to $18.23 in 2028:

GOOG Normalized EPS, Actual and Consensus Estimates: 2023-2028 (TIKR)

That's 69% more in three years.

Investors aren't paying much of a premium for that growth. Microsoft trades at 26x forward earnings, a touch above its one-year average of 25x and well below the 31x it hit last November:

MSFT Stock NTM P/E: 1-Year (TIKR)

At that multiple, the price assumes the profit path holds, with little room for a rule that cuts into it.

title: Dan Ives: Big Tech Free Cash Flow “Will Trough in 1H2027” as Capex Growth Peaks Early
detail:
Dan Ives: Big Tech Free Cash Flow “Will Trough in 1H2027” as Capex Growth Peaks Early
Gian Estrada

AMZN
META
MSFT
GOOG

Trading disclosure
Dan Ives: Big Tech Free Cash Flow "Will Trough in 1H2027" as Capex Growth Peaks Early ©da-kuk from Getty Images Signature and CG6 Images from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. now expects Big Tech's capex growth to peak in 2027, and free cash flow at Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet and Amazon to bottom in the first half of that year.

Analysts' consensus for Microsoft already shows the trough and rebound Ives describes.

Amazon and Meta are deeper in the hole: Meta's third-quarter capex outran its operating cash, and Amazon's free cash flow, on TIKR's measure, fell to $7.7 billion in 2025.

Ives has the bottom about right, but the full payoff still looks like a 2029 story.

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. now thinks the cash squeeze at Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ), Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ), Alphabet (GOOG) and Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) will end sooner than he expected.

In a post on X on Nov. 5, he wrote that "Big Tech capex growth rate now peaks in 2027 vs our previous view that would not happen until 2028/2029." He pointed to the midterm results, especially in Texas, where he expects the data center buildout to slow.

In a follow-up, he tied it to cash: "Free cash flow will trough in 1H2027 and starting in the 2H of next year will start to show a trajectory towards a major rebound in 2028 and massive FCF ramp in 2029-2030."

Bloomberg Intelligence's Mandeep Singh put a number on it. On the Bloomberg Intelligence podcast on Nov. 4, he pointed to Texas data centers and said: "2027 capex could be revised lower by 5 to 7%."

Microsoft's Numbers Already Look Like This

Microsoft's fiscal year ends in June, so its fiscal 2027 includes the first half of 2027, where Ives puts the trough. Analysts expect free cash flow to fall to $34.0 billion that year, about half of fiscal 2026's $67.0 billion, then rebound to $52.3 billion in fiscal 2028.

MSFT Free Cash Flow, Actual and Consensus Estimates: Fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

Microsoft's free cash flow already fell to $18.6 billion in its September quarter from $25.7 billion a year earlier, and a day after that report it sold $25 billion of bonds, its first US investment-grade sale since 2017.

Microsoft was the only one of the five biggest hyperscalers, counting Oracle, whose free cash flow stayed positive in the third quarter.

Amazon and Meta Have the Deeper Hole

On TIKR's measure, Amazon's free cash flow fell to $7.7 billion in 2025, from $32.9 billion in 2024.

AMZN Free Cash Flow: 2021-2025 (TIKR)

Meta's purchases of property and equipment nearly doubled to $69.7 billion in 2025, from $37.3 billion.

META Capital Expenditures: 2021-2025 (TIKR)

Meta's third-quarter capex, including finance-lease principal payments, rose 80% to $34.9 billion, more than the $32.8 billion its operations brought in, and on Oct. 26 it said it plans to sell up to $95 billion of stock. Alphabet burned $9.07 billion of cash in the quarter, according to Reuters.
